items.text: The system shall supervise the tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT, each released every 10 ms in that order, and the task T_DIAG, released after T_OUT in every tenth 10 ms period, as defined by the configuration data.

The system shall take the set of supervised tasks, their periods, their timing limits and their release order from the configuration data, so that a change of these values requires no change of the supervisor code.
The system shall start alive supervision only after the start-up integrity checks have passed.
When a supervised task has not completed an execution for 2 consecutive periods of its own, the system shall detect an alive fault (fault code 1) for that task at the end of the second period.

When a supervised task has not started by the end of its start limit (default 2 ms after its release), that is, its start delay is longer than the start limit, the system shall detect a late start (fault code 2) for that task no later than 100 µs after the end of the start limit; a task that starts at a start delay equal to the start limit, or earlier, is within the limit and is not a late start.
items.rationale: Boundary rule per CON-SUP-127 and SYS-SUP-007: a start at a delay equal to the limit is accepted; the fault condition is a start delay longer than the limit, i.e. no start by the end of the limit. Per CON-SUP-128 and the 100 µs resolution of CON-SUP-127, that condition is detected no later than 100 µs after the end of the limit; verification uses margins of at least 200 µs on either side of the limit.

items.text: When a supervised task has not completed by the end of its execution limit (default 3 ms for T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT, 20 ms for T_DIAG, counted from the start of its execution), that is, its execution time is longer than the execution limit, the system shall detect an overrun (fault code 3) for that task no later than 100 µs after the end of the execution limit; a task that completes at an execution time equal to the execution limit, or earlier, is within the limit and is not an overrun.
items.rationale: Boundary rule per CON-SUP-127 and SYS-SUP-007: completion at an execution time equal to the limit is accepted; the overrun condition is no completion by the end of the limit, i.e. an execution time longer than the limit. With the 100 µs resolution of CON-SUP-127, that condition is detected no later than 100 µs after the end of the limit; verification uses margins of at least 200 µs on either side of the limit.

items.text: The system shall measure start delays and execution times of supervised tasks with a resolution of 100 µs, treating a measured value equal to its limit as within the limit.
items.rationale: Per CON-SUP-127 a violation may be detected up to 100 µs after the limit expires; verification uses margins of at least 200 µs on either side of a limit.

items.text: At the end of each control cycle, when the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle have not arrived in the configured release order or one of them is missing, the system shall detect a program flow fault (fault code 4).

When a program flow fault is detected, the system shall name as entity of the fault report the task expected at the first position, comparing the received checkpoints position by position with the configured release order, where the received checkpoint differs or is missing, with one report per control cycle.

When a configuration value is outside its allowed range (a timing limit longer than the task period, a zero period or an unknown task) at start-up, the system shall detect a configuration fault (fault code 9, entity CONFIG).
The system shall use an independent watchdog, clocked independently of the main clock, with a timeout of 100 ms.
The system shall use a window watchdog that causes a reset when it is refreshed earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after the previous refresh.
While every supervised task is healthy and no fault has been detected, the system shall refresh the window watchdog once per control cycle, at the end of the control cycle.
While every supervised task is healthy and no fault has been detected, the system shall service the independent watchdog at least once within every 100 ms timeout period.

When a fault is detected, except a watchdog reset reported at start-up (fault code 8) whose report alone does not enter the safe state (see SYS-SAFE-011), the system shall stop servicing both watchdogs, without exception, until the next reset.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-121 applies at fault detection; CON-SUP-137 decides that a code 8 report at start-up records a reset that already happened and is not a fault detection in that sense, so servicing continues (SYS-WDG-008). The exception mirrors SYS-SAFE-001. If that report is the third detection of code 8 and the latch is set, SYS-WDG-007 stops servicing.

items.text: When a watchdog reset occurs before the fault report and the safe-state entry of the fault being handled have completed, the system shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low from the reset.
When the third detection of fault code 8 latches the safe state, the system shall stop servicing both watchdogs until the next reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-WDG-005: the start-up code 8 report alone does not stop servicing, but a code 8 detection that sets the latch (SYS-SAFE-007) is a safe-state entry and CON-SUP-121 applies without exception.

items.text: When a watchdog reset is reported at start-up (fault code 8) and it is not the third detection of fault code 8 that latches the safe state, the system shall continue to service both watchdogs as in any start-up.

At start-up, before any supervised task is released, the system shall compute the CRC-32/MPEG-2 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR) over the program code from linker symbol __app_start to __app_end, processing the bytes in increasing address order, and compare it with the little-endian reference word of four bytes stored at linker symbol __app_crc.

At start-up, before any supervised task is released, the system shall compute the CRC-32/MPEG-2 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR) over the configuration data block, processing the bytes in increasing address order, and compare it with the CRC-32 stored with that block as a little-endian reference word of four bytes.

When the CRC-32 of the program code at start-up differs from its reference, the system shall detect a code integrity fault at start-up (fault code 5, entity CODE) at the completion of the computation.

When the CRC-32 of the configuration data block differs from its stored value, the system shall detect a configuration integrity fault (fault code 6, entity CONFIG) at the completion of the computation.
While supervising, the system shall process one 1 KiB segment of the program code with the code check in every control cycle.
The system shall complete a full run-time code check pass over a 1 MiB program image within 11 s.
The system shall limit the processor time used by the run-time code check to 0.5 ms per control cycle.

When the run-time code check finds a mismatch with the reference CRC-32, the system shall detect a code integrity fault at run time (fault code 7, entity CODE) at the completion of the failing integrity computation.

When a fault is detected, except a watchdog reset reported at start-up (fault code 8) whose report alone does not enter the safe state (see SYS-SAFE-011), the system shall enter the safe state, defined as both control outputs driven low and the status signal driven low, within 50 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable by its rule.
When a fault is detected, the system shall have changed the control output pins and the status signal pin to low within 49 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable by its rule.
From any reset until the start-up integrity checks have passed, the system shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low.
After a reset, the system shall configure the two control outputs and the status signal as outputs driven low before any other start-up step.
When the start-up integrity checks have passed and no fault has been detected, the system shall drive the status signal high to show that the controller is operational.

When the system enters the safe state at a detection that is the first or the second of its fault code (per-code count of SYS-SAFE-017), other than fault code 9, the system shall request a software reset within 20 ms after the later of the completion of the fault report and the completion of the safe-state entry.
items.rationale: Fault code 9 (configuration fault at start-up) is excluded because CON-SUP-115 and SYS-SAFE-010 latch the safe state at its first detection until a power-on reset; the reset rule therefore does not apply to it (see SYS-SAFE-014). The reset is requested after the safe-state entry and the fault report (CON-SUP-120). A watchdog reset reported at start-up (fault code 8) does not by itself enter the safe state and start-up continues (CON-SUP-130, SYS-SAFE-011), so the trigger of this item is not met by its first or second detection; this is stated in SYS-SAFE-015.

items.text: While the safe state is latched after a configuration fault (fault code 9) at start-up, the system shall not request a software reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SAFE-006: the reset rule excludes fault code 9, so the absence of a reset after the immediate latch is stated here; the latch holds until a power-on reset per CON-SUP-117.

items.text: When a watchdog reset is reported at start-up (fault code 8) as the first or the second detection of fault code 8, the system shall not request a software reset because of that report.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SAFE-006: CON-SUP-130 makes a start-up code 8 report a report only, without safe-state entry, and start-up continues; the reset of CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-120 follows a safe-state entry, so no reset is requested for these detections. The third detection latches under SYS-SAFE-007.

items.text: When the per-code count of detections of a fault code (SYS-SAFE-017) reaches three, the system shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-140 decides that each fault code keeps its own count (codes 1, 2, 1, 1 latch at the third detection of code 1); the counting rule is SYS-SAFE-017.

items.text: The system shall keep a separate count of detections for each fault code, a detection of a different fault code neither resetting nor advancing it.

When 60 s of fault-free operation, counted within the bounds of SYS-SAFE-008, have been reached since the latest fault detection (SYS-SAFE-019), the system shall return the count of each fault code (SYS-SAFE-017) to zero at that point and at no earlier point.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SAFE-017: the per-code counting rule and the return of a count to zero are separate obligations; the time counted toward the 60 s is bounded by SYS-SAFE-008.

items.text: When a fault is detected, the system shall restart the accumulation of the 60 s of fault-free operation at zero, so that only time counted under SYS-SAFE-008 after the latest fault detection, including across resets, is accumulated and time counted before a detection is never added to time counted after it.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SAFE-018 (finding F-sys-req-set-r6-002): the 60 s must be one uninterrupted fault-free interval; separate intervals must not be summed. The under-count of at most 10 ms per reset and 100 µs per update permitted by SYS-SAFE-008 (CON-SUP-136) is unchanged, so the interval is never over-counted.

items.text: While the safe state is latched after the third detection of the same fault code, the system shall not request a software reset.

The system shall count toward the 60 s of fault-free operation only time spent in the OPERATIONAL state, with an under-count of at most 10 ms per reset and at most 100 µs per update, and never an over-count.
The system shall keep the latch, the fault history, the fault count and the per-code detection counts (SYS-SAFE-017) across software resets and watchdog resets.
The system shall lose the latch, the fault history, the fault count and the per-code detection counts (SYS-SAFE-017) at a loss of power, each count starting at zero after the power-on reset.
When a configuration fault is detected at start-up, the system shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.
When a watchdog reset is reported at start-up (fault code 8), the system shall count it as a detection of fault code 8 for the latch rule of SYS-SAFE-007.

When a watchdog reset is reported at start-up (fault code 8) and it is not the third detection of fault code 8 without 60 s of fault-free operation since the first, the system shall continue start-up without entering the safe state by this report alone.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SAFE-011 (finding F-sys-req-item-r4-001). The third detection latches the safe state under SYS-SAFE-007, LATCHED overriding the other states, so it is excluded here.

items.text: At start-up, the system shall classify the cause of the latest reset from the reset flags as power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor (software) reset or other.
After classifying the reset cause, the system shall send the reset cause in a start-up message on the diagnostic serial line.

When the classified reset cause is independent watchdog or window watchdog, the system shall report a watchdog reset fault (fault code 8) with the entity IWDG or WWDG, the watchdog whose reset flag was set.
The system shall use a diagnostic serial line with 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit.

When a fault is detected, except when a watchdog reset occurs before the transmission has completed (see SYS-DIAG-003), the system shall transmit on the diagnostic serial line a fault report in the form FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> terminated by a line feed, with the codes 1 alive, 2 late start, 3 overrun, 4 flow, 5 code integrity at start-up, 6 configuration integrity, 7 code integrity at run time, 8 watchdog reset and 9 configuration out of range.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-121: no report is required for the fault being handled when a watchdog reset comes before the report and safe-state entry have completed; the exception mirrors SYS-DIAG-003.

items.text: When a fault is detected, the system shall complete the transmission of the fault report within 10 ms of the detection, except when a watchdog reset occurs before the transmission has completed, in which case no report is required for the fault that was being handled.
The system shall use as entity of a fault report the name of the affected task for the fault codes 1, 2 and 3, CODE for the fault codes 5 and 7, and CONFIG for the fault codes 6 and 9.

The system shall give as <ms since start> in a fault report the time of detection of the fault, counted in milliseconds since the latest reset of any kind, as an unsigned decimal number representable in four bytes that wraps to zero after 4294967295 ms.

When the service request GET STATUS is received on the diagnostic serial line, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted (SYS-DIAG-015), the system shall answer STS,<state>,<fault count> within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of the request (SYS-DIAG-013) to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SYS-DIAG-016.

The system shall report as <state> STARTUP from any reset until the start-up checks pass, OPERATIONAL while supervising with no fault, SAFE from the instant a fault is detected, during start-up or operation, until the next reset, a code 8 report at start-up alone not being such a detection and leaving the reported state STARTUP, and LATCHED while the latch is set, LATCHED overriding the other states.
The system shall give as <fault count> the number of fault reports since the last power-on reset.

When the service request GET FAULTS is received, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted (SYS-DIAG-015), the system shall answer within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of the request (SYS-DIAG-013) to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SYS-DIAG-016, with the most recent eight fault reports, or all fault reports when fewer than eight exist, oldest first, one per line, followed by a line END, or only END when none exists.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-139 decides that the service tool sends a request only after the complete previous answer, so the earlier restriction to a request with no unanswered earlier request is dropped; a request received during an answer is excluded from the answer obligation here and discarded without answer (SYS-DIAG-015), as in SYS-DIAG-006, and fault report priority extends the answer time (SYS-DIAG-016, SYS-DIAG-017).

items.text: When a fault report is made while eight fault reports are held, the system shall discard the oldest held fault report and hold the new one, so that the eight most recent fault reports since the last power-on reset are held.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-DIAG-009: CON-SUP-113 requires GET FAULTS to return the last eight fault reports, which needs replacement of the oldest report once eight are held; retention across software and watchdog resets is in SYS-SAFE-009.

items.text: When the service request GET RESET is received, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted (SYS-DIAG-015), the system shall answer RST,<cause> within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of the request (SYS-DIAG-013) to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SYS-DIAG-016, with <cause> the class assigned to the latest reset by SYS-RST-001, given as POR for power-on, IWDG for independent watchdog, WWDG for window watchdog, SW for supervisor (software) reset and OTHER for other.

When any other service request is received, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted (SYS-DIAG-015), the system shall answer ERR within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of the request (SYS-DIAG-013) to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SYS-DIAG-016.
items.rationale: A request received while an earlier answer is being transmitted is excluded from the ERR obligation and discarded without answer (SYS-DIAG-015, CON-SUP-139), as in SYS-DIAG-006, SYS-DIAG-009 and SYS-DIAG-010.

items.text: The system shall accept a service request on the diagnostic serial line as a line of at most 32 ASCII characters ended by a line feed, the request being received when its line feed is received.

When a line longer than 32 characters is received on the diagnostic serial line, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted (SYS-DIAG-015), the system shall answer ERR within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of its line feed to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SYS-DIAG-016.
items.rationale: An overlong line received while an earlier answer is being transmitted is excluded from the ERR obligation and discarded without answer (SYS-DIAG-015, CON-SUP-139), as in SYS-DIAG-006 and SYS-DIAG-011.

items.text: When a service request, or a line longer than 32 characters (SYS-DIAG-014), is received while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted, the system shall discard it without answering it.

When fault reports are transmitted between the receipt of a service request and the end of its answer, the system shall extend the 50 ms answer time of that request by the transmission time of those fault reports.
When a fault report and the answer to a service request are both waiting for transmission on the diagnostic serial line, the system shall transmit the fault report first.

In normal operation (no fault, no service request), the system shall limit the supervisor execution time to 10 % of the processor time over any 1 s window, measured on the simulator at the configured core clock.

From any reset until the software configures the pins, the board shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low by external pull-down resistors, while the corresponding microcontroller pins are inputs.
items.rationale: Platform obligation of CON-SUP-132 supporting SYS-SAFE-003; the software step that follows it is SYS-SAFE-004.

items.text: The supervisor software shall be written in C11 without dynamic memory allocation and without recursion.
The system shall run the supervisor on the Renode simulator with STM32N6 platform descriptions, without the real board.
In test builds, the system shall provide a test hook that injects each fault class (fault codes 1 to 9).
In builds other than test builds, the system shall not contain the fault injection test hooks.

open_points.text: The framing of the start-up message that carries the reset cause (SYS-RST-002) is not defined by the inputs (CON-SUP-111 only says the cause is sent); the text format and terminator are needed. The requirement is verifiable at system level as written.
